sources: The Telegraph (Nov 6), via Haaretz / NV / Times of Israel / Ynet / Times Now relays
fault_line: Trump says Russia gives Iran 'no help at all' -- but Khamenei just sent Putin a personal letter asking for the S-400 shield. Is Moscow about to arm Tehran's air defences, or is this another promise Russia never keeps?

sections.what_happened: [ATTRIBUTED REPORT -- The Telegraph, senior Iranian official] Iran and Russia are negotiating the delivery of S-400 air-defence systems to Tehran; Tehran is 'optimistic' Putin will agree. Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei sent SNSC Secretary Mohsen Rezaei to the Kremlin on Thursday with a personal letter to Putin; the main demand was the S-400. [VERIFIED FACT -- Kremlin meeting confirmed] Putin met Rezaei at the Kremlin on Nov 5 (Times of Israel: Kremlin confirmed the meeting; neither side issued a readout of contents). [ATTRIBUTED REPORT -- The Telegraph, leaked documents] Russian state-owned factories are producing specialised missile-launch equipment for Iran under export contract code 'K-10' (launch units for the LMUR / Product 305 precision missile); a 2024 delivery schedule allocated power units for 90 twin-rail launchers, Iran listed as end customer, shipment due by Dec 2025. [VERIFIED CONTEXT] Iran has sought S-400s for years; Moscow has so far refrained from supplying them for fear of damaging relations with Israel and other regional countries (Telegraph/NV). [CLAIM-BUSTING NOTE] The talks directly contradict Trump's public claim that Russia is providing 'no help' to Iran.
sections.what_verified: 5 distinct declared-tier families (Telegraph T2, Haaretz T3, NV T3, Times of Israel T3, Ynet T3) -- BUT all five trace to the SAME single origin: The Telegraph's Nov 6 report (one unnamed Iranian official + Telegraph-reviewed leaked documents). Repetition of one origin is not independent corroboration. The Rezaei-Putin meeting itself is confirmed (Kremlin, via Times of Israel). The letter's contents and the S-400 request are single-origin. No confirmation from Moscow or Tehran of the S-400 talks.
sections.what_disputed: Neither the Kremlin nor the Iranian government has confirmed the Telegraph's account (israel.com update Nov 7 04:07 Israel time). Moscow has discussed selling S-400s to Tehran for years and has always stopped short; analysts/regional officials cited by NV note Moscow 'promised Iran such systems for years but failed to fulfil those commitments'. The leaked-documents equipment (LMUR launchers) is a separate, older contract (2024 schedule, Dec 2025 delivery) and does not prove an S-400 deal. Talks are not a delivery.
sections.why_matters: While Trump decides on war, Khamenei sent Putin a personal letter asking for the S-400 shield -- the air-defence system that could rebuild Iran's shattered skies. It busts Trump's 'Russia gives no help' claim. Hard number: 90 twin-rail launchers in the leaked contract. Talks, not delivery -- say so.
